title: ID H0727: Amends existing law to revise a provision regarding video voyeurism and to revise a penalty for disclosing explicit synthetic media.

prohibitions: Using, installing or permitting the use or installation of an imaging device at a place where a person has a reasonable expectation of privacy, without the knowledge or consent of the person using such place, with specified sexual or degrading intent (Sec. 18-6605(2))

Intentionally disseminating, publishing or selling, or threatening or conspiring to disseminate, publish or sell, any image of another person who is identifiable and whose intimate areas are exposed or who is engaged in a sexual act, with intent to annoy, terrify, threaten, intimidate, harass, offend, humiliate or degrade, and knowing or reasonably should have known the person understood the image should remain private and did not consent (Sec. 18-6605(3))

Knowingly disclosing explicit synthetic media and knowing or reasonably should know that an identifiable person portrayed did not consent and that disclosure would cause substantial emotional distress (Sec. 18-6606(1)(a))
Disclosing explicit synthetic media with the intent to annoy, terrify, threaten, intimidate, harass, offend, humiliate, or degrade an identifiable person portrayed (Sec. 18-6606(1)(b))
Possessing and threatening to disclose explicit synthetic media with the intent to obtain money or other valuable consideration from an identifiable person portrayed (Sec. 18-6606(1)(c))
reading.what_it_does: Amends Idaho Code Section 18-6605 to revise video voyeurism definitions and prohibitions. Adds Section 18-6606 to criminalize disclosing explicit synthetic media, with misdemeanor and felony penalties. Declares an emergency and sets an effective date of July 1, 2026.
key_definitions: Broadcast: the electronic transmittal of a visual image with the intent that it be viewed by a person or persons (Sec. 18-6605(1)(a))
Disseminate: to make available by any means to any person (Sec. 18-6605(1)(b))
Imaging device: any instrument capable of recording, storing, viewing or transmitting visual images (Sec. 18-6605(1)(c))
Intimate areas: the nude genitals, nude pubic area, nude buttocks or nude female nipple (Sec. 18-6605(1)(d))
Person: any natural person, corporation, partnership, firm, association, joint venture or any other recognized legal entity or any agent or servant thereof (Sec. 18-6605(1)(e))

Place where a person has a reasonable expectation of privacy: a place where a reasonable person would believe that he could undress, be undressed or engage in sexual activity in privacy, without concern that he is being viewed, photographed, filmed or otherwise recorded by an imaging device; or a place where a person might reasonably expect to be safe from casual or hostile surveillance by an imaging device; or any public place where a person, by taking reasonable steps to conceal intimate areas, should be free from the viewing, recording, storing or transmitting of images obtained by imaging devices designed to overcome the barriers created by a person's covering of intimate areas (Sec. 18-6605(1)(f))

Publish: to disseminate with the intent that such image or images be made available by any means to any person; or disseminate with the intent that such images be sold by another person; or post, present, display, exhibit, circulate, advertise or allow access by any means so as to make an image or images available to the public; or disseminate with the intent that an image or images be posted, presented, displayed, exhibited, circulated, advertised or made accessible by any means and to make such image or images available to the public (Sec. 18-6605(1)(g))
Sell: to disseminate to another person, or to publish, in exchange for something of value (Sec. 18-6605(1)(h))

Sexual act: includes, but is not limited to, masturbation; genital, anal or oral sex; sexual penetration with an object; or the transfer or transmission of semen upon any part of the depicted person's body (Sec. 18-6605(1)(i))
Disclose: to make available by any means to any person (Sec. 18-6606(4)(a))

Identifiable individual: a person who is portrayed in whole or in part in synthetic media and who is recognizable by the person's face, likeness, or other distinguishing characteristic, such as a unique birthmark or other recognizable feature (Sec. 18-6606(4)(c))
Intimate parts: the nude genitals, pubic area, anus, or postpubescent female nipple (Sec. 18-6606(4)(d))

Realistically: means that the synthetic media is sufficiently convincing such that an ordinary person viewing the synthetic media would conclude that it is an actual image or video of the identifiable person but does not include drawings, cartoons, or paintings (Sec. 18-6606(4)(e))
Sexual conduct: actual or simulated sexual intercourse, oral-genital contact, manual genital contact, genital-anal contact, oral-anal contact, or other physical-genital contact (Sec. 18-6606(4)(f))

Synthetic media: any image or video created or altered using technical means, such as artificial intelligence, to realistically misrepresent an identifiable individual as engaging in conduct in which the identifiable individual did not engage (Sec. 18-6606(4)(g))
Valuable consideration: includes but is not limited to sexually explicit images or video from the identifiable individual portrayed in the synthetic media (Sec. 18-6606(4)(h))

Passed 2026-03-25. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

Amends Idaho Code Section 18-6605 to revise video voyeurism definitions and prohibitions. Adds Section 18-6606 to criminalize disclosing explicit synthetic media, with misdemeanor and felony penalties. Declares an emergency and sets an effective date of July 1, 2026.

Who it applies to

  • Any person who commits video voyeurism as defined in Sec. 18-6605(2) or (3)
  • Any person who knowingly discloses explicit synthetic media as defined in Sec. 18-6606(1)

Effective date

July 1, 2026

Key definitions

  • Broadcast: the electronic transmittal of a visual image with the intent that it be viewed by a person or persons (Sec. 18-6605(1)(a))
  • Disseminate: to make available by any means to any person (Sec. 18-6605(1)(b))
  • Imaging device: any instrument capable of recording, storing, viewing or transmitting visual images (Sec. 18-6605(1)(c))
  • Intimate areas: the nude genitals, nude pubic area, nude buttocks or nude female nipple (Sec. 18-6605(1)(d))
  • Person: any natural person, corporation, partnership, firm, association, joint venture or any other recognized legal entity or any agent or servant thereof (Sec. 18-6605(1)(e))
  • Place where a person has a reasonable expectation of privacy: a place where a reasonable person would believe that he could undress, be undressed or engage in sexual activity in privacy, without concern that he is being viewed, photographed, filmed or otherwise recorded by an imaging device; or a place where a person might reasonably expect to be safe from casual or hostile surveillance by an imaging device; or any public place where a person, by taking reasonable steps to conceal intimate areas, should be free from the viewing, recording, storing or transmitting of images obtained by imaging devices designed to overcome the barriers created by a person's covering of intimate areas (Sec. 18-6605(1)(f))
  • Publish: to disseminate with the intent that such image or images be made available by any means to any person; or disseminate with the intent that such images be sold by another person; or post, present, display, exhibit, circulate, advertise or allow access by any means so as to make an image or images available to the public; or disseminate with the intent that an image or images be posted, presented, displayed, exhibited, circulated, advertised or made accessible by any means and to make such image or images available to the public (Sec. 18-6605(1)(g))
  • Sell: to disseminate to another person, or to publish, in exchange for something of value (Sec. 18-6605(1)(h))
  • Sexual act: includes, but is not limited to, masturbation; genital, anal or oral sex; sexual penetration with an object; or the transfer or transmission of semen upon any part of the depicted person's body (Sec. 18-6605(1)(i))
  • Disclose: to make available by any means to any person (Sec. 18-6606(4)(a))
  • Explicit synthetic media: synthetic media that depicts or appears to depict an identifiable individual engaged in sexual conduct; the intimate parts of another individual or artificially generated intimate parts presented as the intimate parts of an identifiable individual; or the display or transfer of sexual bodily fluids onto any part of the body of an identifiable individual or from the body of an identifiable individual (Sec. 18-6606(4)(b))
  • Identifiable individual: a person who is portrayed in whole or in part in synthetic media and who is recognizable by the person's face, likeness, or other distinguishing characteristic, such as a unique birthmark or other recognizable feature (Sec. 18-6606(4)(c))
  • Intimate parts: the nude genitals, pubic area, anus, or postpubescent female nipple (Sec. 18-6606(4)(d))
  • Realistically: means that the synthetic media is sufficiently convincing such that an ordinary person viewing the synthetic media would conclude that it is an actual image or video of the identifiable person but does not include drawings, cartoons, or paintings (Sec. 18-6606(4)(e))
  • Sexual conduct: actual or simulated sexual intercourse, oral-genital contact, manual genital contact, genital-anal contact, oral-anal contact, or other physical-genital contact (Sec. 18-6606(4)(f))
  • Synthetic media: any image or video created or altered using technical means, such as artificial intelligence, to realistically misrepresent an identifiable individual as engaging in conduct in which the identifiable individual did not engage (Sec. 18-6606(4)(g))
  • Valuable consideration: includes but is not limited to sexually explicit images or video from the identifiable individual portrayed in the synthetic media (Sec. 18-6606(4)(h))

Obligations

  • not stated in the text

Prohibitions

  • Using, installing or permitting the use or installation of an imaging device at a place where a person has a reasonable expectation of privacy, without the knowledge or consent of the person using such place, with specified sexual or degrading intent (Sec. 18-6605(2))
  • Intentionally disseminating, publishing or selling, or threatening or conspiring to disseminate, publish or sell, any image of another person who is identifiable and whose intimate areas are exposed or who is engaged in a sexual act, with intent to annoy, terrify, threaten, intimidate, harass, offend, humiliate or degrade, and knowing or reasonably should have known the person understood the image should remain private and did not consent (Sec. 18-6605(3))
  • Knowingly disclosing explicit synthetic media and knowing or reasonably should know that an identifiable person portrayed did not consent and that disclosure would cause substantial emotional distress (Sec. 18-6606(1)(a))
  • Disclosing explicit synthetic media with the intent to annoy, terrify, threaten, intimidate, harass, offend, humiliate, or degrade an identifiable person portrayed (Sec. 18-6606(1)(b))
  • Possessing and threatening to disclose explicit synthetic media with the intent to obtain money or other valuable consideration from an identifiable person portrayed (Sec. 18-6606(1)(c))

Penalties and enforcement

The statute creates criminal offenses but does not state which agency enforces them. Video voyeurism is a felony (Sec. 18-6605(4)). Disclosing explicit synthetic media is a misdemeanor unless the identifiable person is under 18 or the person has a prior violation within 5 years, in which case it is a felony punishable by imprisonment up to 10 years, a fine up to $25,000, or both (Sec. 18-6606(2), (3)). No private right of action is stated.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying AI that creates or alters images or videos could be criminally liable if it knowingly discloses explicit synthetic media of an identifiable person without consent and with knowledge or reason to know of substantial emotional distress (Sec. 18-6606(1)(a)).
  • AI systems that generate realistic explicit media of identifiable individuals fall within the definition of synthetic media, which includes images or videos created or altered using technical means such as artificial intelligence (Sec. 18-6606(4)(g)).
  • Organisations that operate as interactive computer services, information services, or telecommunication services are exempt for content provided by another person unless they intentionally aid or abet disclosing explicit synthetic media (Sec. 18-6606(6)).
  • Organisations must avoid using AI to create or disclose explicit synthetic media with intent to harass, threaten, or extort, as those acts are separately prohibited (Sec. 18-6606(1)(b), (c)).

Notable exemptions

  • Interactive computer service, information service, or telecommunication service for content provided by another person, unless the provider intentionally aids or abets video voyeurism (Sec. 18-6605(5)(a))
  • Images involving voluntary exposure in public or commercial settings (Sec. 18-6605(5)(b))
  • Disclosures made in the public interest including reporting unlawful conduct or lawful and common practices of law enforcement, criminal reporting, legal proceedings or medical treatment (Sec. 18-6605(5)(c))
  • Disclosure made for the purpose of a criminal investigation or prosecution that is otherwise lawful (Sec. 18-6606(5)(a))
  • Disclosure for the purpose of, or in connection with, the reporting of unlawful conduct (Sec. 18-6606(5)(b))
  • Explicit synthetic media relates to a matter of public interest and disclosure serves a lawful public purpose, provided that explicit synthetic media does not relate to a matter of public interest merely because a public figure is portrayed (Sec. 18-6606(5)(c))
  • Disclosure for legitimate scientific research or educational purposes (Sec. 18-6606(5)(d))
  • Disclosure made in the normal course of civil legal proceedings and consistent with common practice or protected by court order that prohibits further dissemination (Sec. 18-6606(5)(e))
  • Interactive computer service, information service, or telecommunication service for content provided by another person, unless the provider intentionally aids or abets disclosing explicit synthetic media (Sec. 18-6606(6))

Compliance steps

  • Review AI systems for capability to create or alter images or videos that could constitute explicit synthetic media (Sec. 18-6606(4)(g)).
  • Implement controls to prevent disclosure of explicit synthetic media without consent of the identifiable person (Sec. 18-6606(1)(a)).
  • Prohibit use of AI to create or disclose explicit synthetic media with intent to annoy, terrify, threaten, intimidate, harass, offend, humiliate, or degrade (Sec. 18-6606(1)(b)).
  • Prohibit possession and threats to disclose explicit synthetic media to obtain money or valuable consideration (Sec. 18-6606(1)(c)).
  • If operating as an interactive computer service, information service, or telecommunication service, avoid intentionally aiding or abetting disclosing explicit synthetic media (Sec. 18-6606(6)).
  • For video voyeurism, ensure no use or installation of imaging devices in places where persons have a reasonable expectation of privacy without consent (Sec. 18-6605(2)).
